caseStudy.title: Pre-opening system
caseStudy.lead: How an international hotel kitchen goes from an empty space to its first service, with a team that is ready on day one, not three months later.

meta.v: Kitchen and F&B, linked to every department

caseStudy.ganttNote: Illustrative view of the phases, with no confidential data.
challenge: The hotel opens a complete F&B operation at once. Most of the team comes from different kitchens and works to an international brand standard for the first time.
The goal is not for the team to “find its rhythm” after opening. Every position has to know its job on day one: the same plate, the same standard and the same food safety from the first guest.

steps.d: A competency framework for every kitchen position: what each cook must know and be able to do, and how it is assessed.
For every day before opening it is clear who learns what, with whom, and how progress is checked.
A master plan that aligns the kitchen with service, stewarding, purchasing, engineering and housekeeping.
Readiness programmes: mock services and a soft opening with real pace and real mistakes, before real guests.
Staff certification: every team member is formally signed off for their position before opening.

deliverables: Competency framework and assessment for every position
